test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A man sold a horse at a loss of 7%. Had he been able to sell it at a gain of 9%, it would have fetched ₹6,400 more than it did. The cost price of the horse was:
solution:
**Given:**

Loss percentage = 7%

Gain percentage = 9%

Difference in selling price = ₹6,400

**Formula Used:**

Let the cost price be C.

Selling price at 7% loss = C - 0.07C = 0.93C

Selling price at 9% gain = C + 0.09C = 1.09C

Difference in selling price = 1.09C - 0.93C

**Calculation:**

Given, the difference in selling price is ₹6,400:

⇒ 1.09C - 0.93C = 6,400

⇒ 0.16C = 6,400

⇒ C = 6,400 / 0.16

⇒ C = 40,000

**The cost price of the horse was ₹40,000.**
